title: Residents protest housing costs and mass tourism in Barcelona

tea.why: Residents are protesting skyrocketing housing costs driven by short-term vacation rentals and mass tourism.
tea.want: Demonstrators are demanding affordable housing and an end to mass tourism pressures.
tea.changed: Oct 7: Following the death of an 87-year-old pensioner evicted from her home, thousands took to the streets in multiple Spanish cities including Barcelona.

summary: Following the forced eviction and subsequent death of an 87-year-old pensioner named María del Carmen Abascal, thousands of residents and young people flooded the streets of Barcelona and other Spanish cities. The demonstrators expressed outrage over skyrocketing housing costs and the pressures of mass tourism, which they argue have priced locals out of the housing market through real estate companies converting apartments into vacation rentals. The unrest has targeted the policies of the Socialist Party (PSOE)-Sumar government. While federal and local leaders have attempted to address the affordability crisis through tourism surcharges and statements from officials like Barcelona Mayor Jaume Collboni and Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez, protesters continue to demand systemic change and have called for a general strike.
response: Federal and local governments have tried to implement changes, such as tourism surcharges implemented by Barcelona City Council, while Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez and Barcelona Mayor Jaume Collboni have publicly addressed the housing and tourism crisis.

deaths.text: After she died Oct. 7, thousands took to the streets

updates.text: Thousands took to the streets in Barcelona, Madrid, Valencia and other cities following the death of an 87-year-old evicted pensioner.
Fox News reported that crowds flooded Spanish cities to protest soaring housing costs and mass tourism.
